subject: maths
title: Bar Charts, Pictograms, Tables and Time Graphs
seo_title: Year 4 Bar Charts and Time Graphs Worksheets: Pictograms, Tally Charts and Tables (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Interpret and present discrete and continuous data using appropriate graphical methods, including bar charts and time graphs; solve comparison, sum and difference problems using information presented in bar charts, pictograms, tables and other graphs.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on statistics: read bar charts with scales of 2, 5 and 10, pictograms with half symbols, tally charts, tables and time graphs, then solve sum and difference problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Check the scale or the key first. Then read the graph.
key_sub: A bar halfway between 10 and 20 shows 15. Half a symbol is half of the key. On a time graph, go up from the time and across to the scale. Altogether means add; how many more means subtract.
body_html:
Four ways to show data

Data is information we collect, such as votes or temperatures. A tally chart helps you count. A table shows the numbers. A bar chart or pictogram lets you compare groups at a glance. A time graph shows how something changes over time.

Read a bar chart

First find what the scale goes up in: 2s, 5s or 10s. Then follow the top of the bar across to the scale. If a bar ends halfway between two lines, the value is halfway between the two numbers.

Example

How many more pupils have a dog than a rabbit?

Dog: 12. Rabbit: 9. 12 − 9 = 3.

Answer: 3 more pupils

Read a pictogram

Look at the key first. Count the symbols in a row and multiply by the key. Half a symbol stands for half of the key, not 1.

Example

How many votes did Orange get?

1 whole circle and half a circle: 4 + 2 = 6.

Answer: 6 votes

Tally charts and tables

In a tally chart, every fifth mark goes across the other four. Count the groups in 5s, then add the single marks.

In a table, find the right row, then go across to the right column.

DayYear 3Year 4
Monday1825
Tuesday2216
Example

How many books did Year 4 borrow on Monday?

Monday row, Year 4 column: 25.

Answer: 25 books

Read a time graph

A time graph shows continuous data, like temperature or height, that keeps changing. The points are joined with lines because the value changes between the times too. Go up from the time to the line, then across to the scale.

Example

How much warmer was it at 12:00 than at 10:00?

12:00: 14 °C. 10:00: 8 °C. 14 − 8 = 6.

Answer: 6 °C

Sum or difference?

The question saysDo this
altogether, in total, both together, A or BAdd (sum)
how many more, how many fewer, difference, how much warmerSubtract (difference)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading a bar between two lines as the lower lineHalfway between 10 and 20 is 15
Counting symbols instead of using the key (5 circles = 5)Multiply by the key: 5 × 4 = 20
Saying half a symbol = 1Half a symbol is half of the key
Counting a tally group of 5 as 4The line across is the fifth mark
Reading a time graph at the wrong timeGo straight up from the time on the bottom axis
Adding when the question asks how many moreHow many more means subtract

faq.q: What statistics do children learn in Year 4?
faq.a: In Year 4 pupils read and draw bar charts, pictograms, tables and time graphs. They use them to answer comparison, sum and difference questions, such as how many more or how many altogether.

A time graph is a line graph that shows how something changes over time, such as the temperature during a day or the height of a plant each week. Time goes along the bottom and the points are joined with straight lines.

faq.q: What is the difference between discrete and continuous data?
faq.a: Discrete data is counted in whole groups, such as votes or pets, and suits a bar chart or pictogram. Continuous data, such as temperature, height or distance, keeps changing and suits a time graph.

faq.q: How do you read half a symbol on a pictogram?
faq.a: Half a symbol stands for half of the key. If each circle = 10 pupils, half a circle = 5 pupils, so 3 and a half circles = 35 pupils.

sets.title: Read bar charts with scales of 2, 5 and 10

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many votes did Purple get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Purple bar ends on the line for 30. So the answer is 30 votes.

items.q: How many votes did Autumn get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Autumn bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. So the answer is 35 votes.

items.q: How many robins were seen?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Robin bar ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. So the answer is 9 birds.

items.q: How many pupils chose cricket?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Cricket bar ends on the line for 30. So the answer is 30 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows 35 votes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 35 on the scale. The Orange bar ends on the line for 35.

items.q: How many stickers has Kai got?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Kai bar ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it shows 7. So the answer is 7 stickers.

items.q: How many orange lollies were sold?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Orange bar ends on the line for 70. So the answer is 70 lollies.

items.q: Which bar shows the most trees?
items.e: The Birch bar is the longest one. The Birch bar ends on the line for 25. It shows 25 trees.

items.q: How many pupils have a dog?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Dog bar ends halfway between 4 and 6, so it shows 5. So the answer is 5 pupils.

items.q: How many Sport books were borrowed?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Sport bar ends on the line for 70. So the answer is 70 books.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 10, 20, 30 … Each line is 10 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 10s.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest shells?
items.e: The Ava bar is the shortest one. The Ava bar ends on the line for 4. It shows 4 shells.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Friday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Fri bar ends on the line for 25. So the answer is 25 cakes.

items.q: How many books did Isla read?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Isla bar ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it shows 7. So the answer is 7 books.

items.q: Which bar shows 25 pupils?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Find 25 on the scale. The Roast bar ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25.

items.q: How many cans did class 4D collect?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The 4D bar ends on the line for 60. So the answer is 60 cans.

items.q: Which bar shows the most votes?
items.e: The Spring bar is the longest one. The Spring bar ends on the line for 30. It shows 30 votes.

items.q: How many stickers has Mohammed got?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Mohammed bar ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it shows 7. So the answer is 7 stickers.

items.q: Which bar shows 10 points?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 10 on the scale. The Owl bar ends on the line for 10.

items.q: How many shells did Maya find?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 shells. The Maya row has 2 circles: 2 × 2 = 4 shells.
Look at the key: each star stands for 4 lollies. The Cola row has 4 stars and half a star: 4 × 4 = 16, and half of 4 is 2, so 16 + 2 = 18 lollies.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 4 books. Half a square is half of 4, which is 2 books, not 1.

items.q: How many cans did class 4D collect?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 10 cans. The 4D row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 cans.
Every star stands for the same number, so the row with the most stars shows the most. The Isla row has 6 stars: 6 × 4 = 24 books.

items.q: How many pupils have a cat?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 pupils. The Cat row has 2 squares: 2 × 2 = 4 pupils.

items.q: Each star stands for 4 books. Freya read 18 books. How many stars should be in her row?
items.e: 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2. 2 is half of 4, so draw 4 stars and half a star. Check: 4 × 4 + 2 = 18.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 pupils. The Bus row has 2 stars and half a star: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 pupils.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 pupils. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 pupils, not 1.

items.q: Which row shows 14 birds?
items.e: 14 birds ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 2, so look for 3 and a half circles. The Blackbird row has 3 circles and half a circle: 3 × 4 = 12, and half of 4 is 2, so 12 + 2 = 14 birds.
Look at the key: each star stands for 4 cakes. The Thu row has 2 stars: 2 × 4 = 8 cakes.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 pupils. 45 pupils walk to school. How many circles should be in the Walk row?
items.e: 45 ÷ 10 = 4 remainder 5. 5 is half of 10, so draw 4 circles and half a circle. Check: 4 × 10 + 5 = 45.

items.q: How many votes did Red get?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 votes. The Red row has 1 circle and half a circle: 1 × 2 = 2, and half of 2 is 1, so 2 + 1 = 3 votes.
Every star stands for the same number, so the row with the fewest stars shows the fewest. The Oak row has 1 star: 1 × 10 = 10 trees.

items.q: How many pupils chose swimming?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 10 pupils. The Swimming row has 2 squares and half a square: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 pupils.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 4 votes. Half a circle is half of 4, which is 2 votes, not 1.
Look at the key: each star stands for 4 birds. The Sparrow row has 5 stars and half a star: 5 × 4 = 20, and half of 4 is 2, so 20 + 2 = 22 birds.

items.q: Which row shows 5 pupils?
items.e: 5 pupils ÷ 2 = 2 remainder 1, so look for 2 and a half squares. The Cricket row has 2 squares and half a square: 2 × 2 = 4, and half of 2 is 1, so 4 + 1 = 5 pupils.

items.q: Each square stands for 2 votes. Summer got 13 votes. How many squares should be in the Summer row?
items.e: 13 ÷ 2 = 6 remainder 1. 1 is half of 2, so draw 6 squares and half a square. Check: 6 × 2 + 1 = 13.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 books. The Mystery row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 10 = 30, and half of 10 is 5, so 30 + 5 = 35 books.

items.q: How many red cars were there?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Red row has 2 groups of 5 and 1 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: How many white cars were there?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The White row has 3 groups of 5 and 1 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 1 = 16.

items.q: How many cars went past the school?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Car row has 3 groups of 5 and 3 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 3 = 18.

items.q: Which row shows 8 vehicles?
items.e: 8 = 5 + 3. Look for 1 group of 5 and 3 single marks. That is the Bus row.

items.q: How many votes did Banana get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Banana row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: How many votes are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Apple 10, Banana 13, Grapes 23, Pear 7. Then add: 10 + 13 + 23 + 7 = 53 votes.

items.q: How many blackbirds were seen?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Blackbird row has 1 group of 5 and 2 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 2 = 7.

items.q: What is the difference between the biggest and the smallest number of birds?
items.e: The biggest is Magpie (22). The smallest is Sparrow (5). Difference means subtract: 22 − 5 = 17.

items.q: Which row shows 8 pupils?
items.e: 8 = 5 + 3. Look for 1 group of 5 and 3 single marks. That is the Cricket row.

items.q: How many pupils are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Football 5, Netball 12, Swimming 13, Cricket 8. Then add: 5 + 12 + 13 + 8 = 38 pupils.

items.q: How many books did Year 3 borrow on Wednesday?
items.e: Find the Wednesday row, then go across to the Year 3 column. The cell says 23.

items.q: How many books were borrowed on Thursday altogether?
items.e: Add the two cells in the Thursday row: 33 + 16 = 49.

items.q: On Tuesday, how many more books did Year 4 borrow than Year 3?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 21 − 8 = 13.

items.q: On which day were the most books borrowed altogether?
items.e: Add each row: Mon 53, Tue 29, Wed 42, Thu 49. The biggest total is 53 on Monday.

items.q: How many books did Year 3 borrow on Tuesday?
items.e: Find the Tuesday row, then go across to the Year 3 column. The cell says 8.

items.q: How many books did Year 3 borrow from Monday to Thursday?
items.e: Add the whole Year 3 column: 32 + 8 + 17 + 14 = 71.

items.q: On Monday, how many more books did Year 3 borrow than Year 4?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 32 − 18 = 14.

items.q: How many books did Year 4 borrow on Thursday?
items.e: Find the Thursday row, then go across to the Year 4 column. The cell says 19.

items.q: How many books were borrowed on Monday altogether?
items.e: Add the two cells in the Monday row: 33 + 25 = 58.

items.q: How many books did Year 3 borrow from Monday to Thursday?
items.e: Add the whole Year 3 column: 33 + 26 + 23 + 35 = 117.

items.q: What was the temperature at 11:00?
items.e: Go up from 11:00 to the point, then across to the scale. The scale goes up in 2s. At 11:00 the point is halfway between the lines for 12 and 14, so it shows 13 °C.

items.q: How tall was the sunflower in week 2?
items.e: Go up from week 2 to the point, then across to the scale. The scale goes up in 2s. At week 2 the point is halfway between the lines for 4 and 6, so it shows 5 cm.

items.q: How far had the car travelled at 10:10?
items.e: Go up from 10:10 to the point, then across to the scale. The scale goes up in 10s. At 10:10 the point is halfway between the lines for 0 and 10, so it shows 5 km.

items.q: What was the temperature of the tea after 50 minutes?
items.e: Go up from 50 minutes to the point, then across to the scale. The scale goes up in 10s. At 50 minutes the point is halfway between the lines for 30 and 40, so it shows 35 °C.

items.q: What was the temperature at 13:00?
items.e: Go up from 13:00 to the point, then across to the scale. The scale goes up in 2s. At 13:00 the point is halfway between the lines for 16 and 18, so it shows 17 °C.

items.q: At what time was it warmest?
items.e: Find the highest point on the line. It is at 13:00, when it was 17 °C.

items.q: In which week did the sunflower first reach 11 cm?
items.e: Find 11 on the scale and go across until you meet the line. Then go down: it is week 3.

items.q: How much warmer was it at 15:00 than at 09:00?
items.e: Read both points: 7 °C at 09:00 and 11 °C at 15:00. Find the difference: 11 − 7 = 4 °C.

items.q: By how much did the tea cool down between 10 and 50 minutes?
items.e: Read both points: 70 °C at 10 minutes and 25 °C at 50 minutes. Find the difference: 70 − 25 = 45 °C.

items.q: The car stopped for a break. Between which two times was it not moving?
items.e: When the car stops, the distance does not change, so the line is flat. From 10:40 to 10:50 the distance stays at 45 km.

items.q: How much did the sunflower grow from week 1 to week 4?
items.e: Read both points: 3 cm at week 1 and 11 cm at week 4. Find the difference: 11 − 3 = 8 cm.

items.q: At what time was it warmest?
items.e: Find the highest point on the line. It is at 14:00, when it was 18 °C.

items.q: How far did the car travel between 10:30 and 10:50?
items.e: Read both points: 20 km at 10:30 and 45 km at 10:50. Find the difference: 45 − 20 = 25 km.

items.q: Between which two weeks did the sunflower grow the most?
items.e: Look for the steepest part of the line. From week 2 to week 3 it goes up 11 − 7 = 4 cm. No other part goes up as much.

items.q: By how much did the tea cool down between 0 and 50 minutes?
items.e: Read both points: 85 °C at 0 minutes and 35 °C at 50 minutes. Find the difference: 85 − 35 = 50 °C.

items.q: At what time did the temperature first reach 13 °C?
items.e: Find 13 on the scale and go across until you meet the line. Then go down: it is 13:00.

items.q: Estimate the temperature at 11:30.
items.e: 11:30 is halfway between 11:00 and 12:00. The line goes from 11 °C to 15 °C, so halfway is about 13 °C. A time graph lets you read values between the points.

items.q: How much did the sunflower grow from week 0 to week 2?
items.e: Read both points: 1 cm at week 0 and 5 cm at week 2. Find the difference: 5 − 1 = 4 cm.

items.q: Estimate the distance the car had travelled at 10:05.
items.e: 10:05 is halfway between 10:00 and 10:10. The line goes from 0 km to 10 km, so halfway is about 5 km. A time graph lets you read values between the points.

items.q: Between which two times did the temperature rise the most?
items.e: Look for the steepest part of the line. From 09:00 to 10:00 it goes up 11 − 8 = 3 °C. No other part goes up as much.

sets.title: Word problems: sum, difference and comparison

items.q: Year 4 want to collect 200 cans for the food bank. How many more cans do they need?
items.e: Step 1: cans so far: 40 + 25 + 55 + 30 = 150. Step 2: 200 − 150 = 50. (Reading the 4B bar as 20 or 30 gives a wrong total.)
Each star = 4 books, so half a star = 2. Amelia: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. Isla: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10. Altogether means add: 14 + 10 = 24.

items.q: How many more cakes were sold on Friday than on Monday?
items.e: Each circle = 10 cakes, so half a circle = 5. Friday: 5 × 10 = 50. Monday: 2 × 10 + 5 = 25. How many more means subtract: 50 − 25 = 25.

items.q: Each cake costs 50p. How much money did the cake sale make on Tuesday?
items.e: Tuesday: 4 circles × 10 = 40 cakes. 2 cakes cost 50p + 50p = £1, so 40 cakes cost 40 ÷ 2 = £20.

items.q: How many tickets were sold altogether?
items.e: Add all four cells: 46 + 38 = 84 on Thursday and 62 + 54 = 116 on Friday. 84 + 116 = 200.

items.q: Adult tickets cost £5 each. How much money did the adult tickets make on Friday?
items.e: Friday adult tickets: 62. 62 × 5 = 300 + 10 = £310. (54 is the child tickets, not the adult tickets.)

items.q: How many more cars went past than buses and lorries together?
items.e: Cars: 4 groups of 5 and 3 more = 23. Buses and lorries together: 7 + 9 = 16. Difference: 23 − 16 = 7.

items.q: The chart shows all 30 days of April. The class played outside at lunchtime on every day that was not rainy. On how many days did they play outside?
items.e: Step 1: the Rainy bar ends on the line for 8, so 8 days were rainy. Step 2: 30 − 8 = 22 days. Check: 12 + 7 + 3 = 22.

items.q: The journey to the seaside is 80 km. How much further did the car still have to go at 10:30?
items.e: At 10:30 the point is on the line for 30, so the car had travelled 30 km. Still to go: 80 − 30 = 50 km.

items.q: How much warmer was the warmest time of the day than 09:00?
items.e: The warmest point is 16 °C at 13:00. At 09:00 it was 7 °C. Difference: 16 − 7 = 9 °C.

items.q: Poppy planted the sunflower in week 0. How much did it grow in the 6 weeks?
items.e: Week 0: 3 cm. Week 6: 18 cm. It grew 18 − 3 = 15 cm. 18 cm is how tall it is, not how much it grew.

items.q: Which data would be best shown on a time graph?
items.e: A time graph shows something that changes over time, like temperature. Fruits, pets and ways to school are groups you count, so a bar chart or pictogram is better.

items.q: Oliver measures his bean plant every week. Which graph should he use to show how it grows?
items.e: Height keeps changing over time, even between his measurements. A time graph joins the points so you can see it grow.

items.q: Which data is best shown in a bar chart, not a time graph?
items.e: Favourite sports are separate groups that you count. Temperature, height and mass change over time, so they suit a time graph.

items.q: 30 pupils voted altogether. The bar for cricket is missing. How many pupils chose cricket?
items.e: Step 1: add the other bars: 9 + 6 + 8 = 23. Step 2: 30 − 23 = 7 pupils chose cricket. (Football ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it is 9, not 8.)

items.q: How many more points does Hawk House need to catch up with Falcon House?
items.e: Falcon: 80. Hawk: 45 (halfway between 40 and 50). 80 − 45 = 35 points.

items.q: The school bought 50 pieces of fruit. The tally chart shows the fruit that pupils took. How many pieces were left?
items.e: Pupils took 14 + 9 + 6 + 11 = 40 pieces. Left: 50 − 40 = 10 pieces. (Counting each group of 5 as 4 gives 34 and a wrong answer of 16.)

items.q: Lily waits until her tea is below 60 °C. After how many minutes is the tea first below 60 °C?
items.e: At 20 minutes the tea is exactly 60 °C, which is not below 60 °C. At 30 minutes it is 50 °C, so the answer is 30 minutes.

items.q: How many pupils walk or cycle to school?
items.e: Walk: 35. Bike: 25. “Walk or cycle” means put them together: 35 + 25 = 60 pupils.

items.q: How many birds were seen altogether?
items.e: Each square = 2 birds, so half a square = 1. Robin 5, blackbird 8, sparrow 11, blue tit 6. 5 + 8 + 11 + 6 = 30 birds.
